proposals.before: The Gaoyang era knew it as Youling; Yao as Youdu; Shun carved out Youzhou.
proposals.after: The Gaoyang clan called it Youling; Yao called it Youdu; Shun carved out Youzhou.
proposals.reason: 高陽氏 denotes the Gaoyang clan/person, not an impersonal "era"; keep the personal agent parallel to Yao and Shun.

proposals.before: An Lushan, Shi Siming, Li Huaishan, Zhu Tao, Liu Cong, and Liu Ji carved it out one after another.
proposals.after: An Lushan, Shi Siming, Li Huaishan, Zhu Tao, Liu Peng, and Liu Ji carved it out one after another.
proposals.reason: 劉怦 is read Liu Peng (Pēng); Cong does not match the character 怦.

proposals.before: An Lushan, Shi Siming, Li Huaishan, Zhu Tao, Liu Cong, Liu Ji seized the region in succession.
proposals.after: An Lushan, Shi Siming, Li Huaishan, Zhu Tao, Liu Peng, Liu Ji seized the region in succession.
proposals.reason: 劉怦 is read Liu Peng (Pēng); Cong does not match the character 怦.

proposals.before: Liu Rengong erected palaces and shrines on Daan Mountain; Wang Ruone instructed the court in alchemy; a portion of Jixian was detached to provision them.
proposals.after: Liu Rengong erected palaces and shrines on Daan Mountain and studied alchemy and immortal arts from the fangshi Wang Ruone; he therefore detached part of Jixian to provision them.
proposals.reason: 師…於方士王若訥 means Liu Rengong learned those arts FROM Wang Ruone, not that Wang instructed "the court".

proposals.before: Liu Rengong built palaces and shrines on Daan Mountain; the master Wang Ruone taught elixir and ascension arts to the court; Jixian was split off to supply them.
proposals.after: Liu Rengong built palaces and shrines on Daan Mountain; he studied elixir and ascension arts under the fangshi Wang Ruone; he therefore split off Jixian to supply them.
proposals.reason: 師…於 marks Liu as the student of Wang Ruone; the literal reverses the teacher-student direction.

proposals.before: Wang Zeng's Account of Service to the Khitan records: "From Xiongzhou's Baima post, forty li by ferry to Xincheng County, the old Dukang Pavilion site.
proposals.after: Wang Zeng's Account of Service to the Khitan records: "From Xiongzhou's Baigou post, forty li by ferry to Xincheng County, the old Dukang Pavilion site.
proposals.reason: 白溝驛 is Baigou Relay, not Baima (白馬).

proposals.before: Song minister Wang Zeng, Account of Presenting Matters to the Khitan, says: "From Xiongzhou Baima post one crosses the river; forty li to Xincheng County, ancient Dukang Pavilion ground.
proposals.after: Song minister Wang Zeng, Account of Presenting Matters to the Khitan, says: "From Xiongzhou Baigou post one crosses the river; forty li to Xincheng County, ancient Dukang Pavilion ground.
proposals.reason: 白溝驛 is Baigou Relay, not Baima (白馬).

proposals.before: Outside the south gate is the Prince of Yu Wang's office, a place for banquets.
proposals.after: Outside the south gate is the Prince of Yu's hall, a place for banquets.
proposals.reason: 於越王廨 is the uyug/Prince of Yu hall; "Yu Wang's" double-renders 王 and obscures the title.
固安縣 is Gu'an County; Guan omits the apostrophe and mismatches the established romanization of 固安.

proposals.before: Sui Kaihuang year 9 moved the seat from Yizhou Laishui to Youzhou under the old Guan County name.
proposals.after: Sui Kaihuang year 9 moved the seat from Yizhou Laishui to Youzhou under the old Gu'an County name.
proposals.reason: 漢故安縣名 refers to Gu'an (故安/固安); Guan is an incomplete romanization of 故安.

proposals.before: Taizu raided Ding, took Xingtang, and relocated the entire populace north to Tan Prefecture on open ground; ten stockades were founded and the name Xingtang kept.
proposals.after: Taizu raided Ding Prefecture, took Xingtang, and relocated the entire populace north to Tan Prefecture on open ground; ten stockades were founded and the name Xingtang kept.
proposals.reason: Chinese 定州 is Ding Prefecture; idiomatic 'Ding' alone drops the administrative unit present in the source and literal.

proposals.before: Tang Dali year 4 carved it from Guan County, then abolished it.
proposals.after: Tang Dali year 4 carved it from Gu'an County, then abolished it.
proposals.reason: 固安縣 is Gu'an County; Guan is an incomplete romanization inconsistent with Gu'an used elsewhere in this chapter.

proposals.before: Sui Kaihuang year 16 founded the present seat at the northwest corner of old Guan town.
proposals.after: Sui Kaihuang year 16 founded the present seat at the northwest corner of old Gu'an town.
proposals.reason: 故安城 is old Gu'an town; Guan drops the standard romanization of 故安/固安.

proposals.before: Formerly the Spring and Autumn state of Wuzhongzi.
proposals.after: Formerly the Spring and Autumn state of the Viscount of Wuzhong.
proposals.reason: 無終子國 names the polity of the Viscount of Wuzhong (無終子), not a place-name 'Wuzhongzi'.

proposals.before: Originally the Spring and Autumn Wuzhongzi state.
proposals.after: Originally the Spring and Autumn state of the Viscount of Wuzhong.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise fuses 無終子 into 'Wuzhongzi' instead of rendering the titled ruler's state.

proposals.before: When Duke Huan of Qi attacked the Mountain Rong he met the mountain spirit Yu—here.
proposals.after: When Duke Huan of Qi attacked the Mountain Rong he met the mountain spirit Yu—this is that place.
proposals.reason: Chinese 即此 means 'this is that place'; the em-dash fragment '—here' is unclear English.

proposals.before: There is Fusu Spring, very sweet; Qin crown prince Fusu, building the Long Wall northward, once encamped here;
proposals.after: There is Fusu Spring, very sweet; Qin crown prince Fusu, while building the Long Wall in the north, once encamped here;
proposals.reason: Chinese 北築長城 means building the Long Wall in the north; 'building the Long Wall northward' is awkward and slightly misleading.
